translation_provenance: Direct Kyrgyz-to-English draft from source extraction and all twenty PDF page images. No prior English translation or translation service used. Edition glossary and primary dictionaries consulted; interpretation and uncertainties recorded per source ID. No independent specialist review.

notes.manas-2010:p0698:b001:l001: Буурсун: wooden plow, confirmed by edition glossary1836:l020 and following line; the farming image is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0698:b001:l010: Кылым here the peoples/world's affairs, not a chronological century count.
notes.manas-2010:p0698:b001:l012: Кара саат: Yudakhin саатI gives a troublesome/dangerous person; the1969 dictionary gives malicious intention. Scourge conveys the hostile epithet; not clock/hour or a literal dark time.
notes.manas-2010:p0698:b001:l022: Биттеп is castration here, with the monks in the preceding row as its object; the violent humiliation is explicit in the source.
notes.manas-2010:p0698:b001:l032: Орго and Дөңгөгө are treated as personal names; their historical identification is not established here.
notes.manas-2010:p0699:b001:l013: Бээлебей provisionally read as failing to take control; exact force in this flight description remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0699:b001:l024: Капканын is read as the possessive/accusative of city gate in context, rather than a hunting trap.
notes.manas-2010:p0700:b001:l011: Чоң Билер retained as a named chief sorcerer. The shift from third-person introduction to first-person speech in the following rows remains.
notes.manas-2010:p0700:b001:l012: Боконо: lower/false ribs, supported by Yudakhin бокон entry; not collarbone.
notes.manas-2010:p0700:b001:l013: The source explicitly describes bowels filling with excrement from fear. Register retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0700:b001:l024: Баалап provisionally rendered carefully chosen for the loaded possessions; no emendation to a binding verb is made.
notes.manas-2010:p0700:b001:l040: Күлкана retained as a name in the comparison; identity and precise name form remain uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0701:b001:l012: Сорду retains the sucking-dry image in Alöökö's hostile account despite the conventional magnanimous epithet.
notes.manas-2010:p0702:b001:l004: Бил is elephant here: hide used for the great drum, not waist or know.
notes.manas-2010:p0702:b001:l007: КериI in Yudakhin refers to the slopes, linked to керүү; not a city wall. The preceding movement is the drum's hyperbolic effect.
notes.manas-2010:p0702:b001:l013: Тыргоот retained as the Torgut ethnonym, without modern ethnic adjudication.
notes.manas-2010:p0702:b001:l023: Printed Өлчөсө каның муну айтып is syntactically awkward. Provisionally considering/after measuring; no silent replacement of Өлчөсө with a person's name.
notes.manas-2010:p0702:b001:l024: Атаңдын көрү is a curse invoking the father's grave, retained literally rather than omitted.
notes.manas-2010:p0703:b001:l005: Окто is a halter in this preparation of horses, not loading a gun; Yudakhin usage checked in earlier batch research.
notes.manas-2010:p0703:b001:l028: Walnuts are targets in a knucklebone-style shooting/flicking game; no firearm is added.
notes.manas-2010:p0703:b001:l031: Ат капталдан той retained as a feast beside horses. A more specific idiomatic institution is unverified.
notes.manas-2010:p0704:b001:l007: Көөр interpreted as precious stones; edition glossary1839:l030 links көөхар/көөр to асыл таш.
notes.manas-2010:p0704:b001:l008: Көк күбө is blue mail, distinguished from the soft protective garment күпү.
notes.manas-2010:p0704:b001:l025: Жорго retained as a pacing horse; not a generic trotter.
notes.manas-2010:p0704:b001:l028: Беренжи: Yudakhin берен entry gives fabric and a beldemchi-like battle wrap with the exact салын- construction. Edition glossary1835:l007–009 instead describes a saddle cover. Battle wrap is selected from the clothing context; material and construction remain uncertain, not asserted to be metal armor.
notes.manas-2010:p0704:b001:l031: Карыпчы rendered armguard, following the contextual shared glossary.
notes.manas-2010:p0704:b001:l034: Буулум retained as satin cloth; precise weave is not established from this line.
notes.manas-2010:p0704:b001:l038: The red elephant is retained literally; no horse is substituted.
notes.manas-2010:p0705:b001:l004: Алдыңкы is front, not automatically lower, in the grotesque lip description.
notes.manas-2010:p0705:b001:l012: Кара байыр is the Karabayyr horse type; treated as an identified breed/type name, not an untranslated ordinary noun.
notes.manas-2010:p0705:b001:l026: Анжы retained as the printed place-name form Anjy, possibly related to Andijan; not silently expanded.
notes.manas-2010:p0705:b001:l031: Дилде rendered gold coins, without assigning a modern denomination or value.
notes.manas-2010:p0705:b001:l033: Шири describes leather vessels in the carried-wealth list.
notes.manas-2010:p0706:b001:l002: Бакалап provisionally describes picking one's way; the precise motion remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0706:b001:l008: The hundred-strong organization is retained alongside the fifty-strong organization below; no numerical harmonization.
notes.manas-2010:p0706:b001:l012: The fifty-strong units are explicit and retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0706:b001:l014: Чайла- means become exhausted/lose strength in Yudakhin and1969/2015 dictionaries, with animal examples. Corrected to weakening; not tea-drinking, watering, or feeding.
notes.manas-2010:p0706:b001:l040: Арам өлүм conveyed as a wretched death; no technical legal judgment is added.
notes.manas-2010:p0707:b001:l006: Кокон кан read as khan of Kokand; the proper-name/title construction remains potentially ambiguous.
notes.manas-2010:p0707:b001:l025: Жаман суу rendered bad waters literally; it may also function as the place name Jaman-Suu.
notes.manas-2010:p0707:b001:l030: Жылгын-Талаа and Таш-Кечүү retained as place names, not mapped onto unverified modern coordinates.
notes.manas-2010:p0707:b001:l032: Маш conveys familiarity/proficiency in crossing the terrain.
notes.manas-2010:p0707:b001:l034: Куюлган provisionally describes crumbling/poured terrain at Ak-Zhar; exact landform remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l006: The source explicitly says eighty-four equipped men. Forty-companion formulas and five groups of ten elsewhere are also retained without reconciliation.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l011: Кош бадана торгой көз: double mail with rings compared to larks' eyes; exact manufacture is not reconstructed.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l018: Sieve lungs and copper forelegs are literal heroic horse epithets.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l023: Hoe-shaped croup and stone hooves are retained as the source's horse imagery.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l028: Керней and сурнай distinguished as trumpet and shawm, rather than one generic instrument.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l035: Ырапыс: ribbed/rep cloth, confirmed by edition glossary1844:l006.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l036: Көк чолок translated descriptively as short-tailed blue-gray; also usable as the steed name Kök Cholok.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l039: The dun horse follows Bakay's blue-gray mount. Possible implicit change of rider is left unstated rather than assigning both mounts to Bakay.
notes.manas-2010:p0708:b001:l042: First group of ten, skilled spearmen. Four further groups of ten follow; the source's forty refrain is retained independently.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l004: Second ten, swordsmen; not reconciled with the forty-companion formula.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l005: The parenthesized printed verse is translated and counted, not treated as apparatus.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l009: Third group of ten, battle-axe fighters, retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l013: Fourth group of ten, bowmen, retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l015: Fifth group of ten, marksmen, retained; no division into an invented total of forty.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l016: Канкор rendered blood-stained as a conventional martial epithet; the violence is not softened into merely brave.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l023: The eighteen thousand worlds are the explicit cosmological formula, not a verified count of terrestrial places.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l030: Ала көөдөн read as rash/impetuous, contrasted with the wise men.
notes.manas-2010:p0709:b001:l040: The comparison to a bereaved wife is explicit in the source and retained as the narrator's simile.
notes.manas-2010:p0710:b001:l008: Кулача interpreted as dun-colored; the formula is retained despite differently colored mounts in adjacent descriptions.
notes.manas-2010:p0710:b001:l010: Көйкашка denotes white-blazed horses in this context; not the figurative outstanding-person sense.
notes.manas-2010:p0710:b001:l021: Сан кол denotes an immense/countless host here; no unprinted exact number is assigned.
notes.manas-2010:p0710:b001:l023: Букта provisionally expresses a firm grip in spear-handling; exact adverbial nuance remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0710:b001:l029: Чайдос is a tea vessel/teapot, supported by Abramzon's Kyrgyz ethnography description of кашкар чайник/чайдос. The gold/cheap-tea contrast is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0710:b001:l035: Азган-тозгон retained as scattered/impoverished, despite the celebratory warrior description around it.
notes.manas-2010:p0711:b001:l003: Кыягы rendered mettle/quality in the warrior predicate, not a musical instrument; exact shade remains provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0711:b001:l012: The grass-to-fire substitution is the source's hyperbolic escalation, not a translation reversal.
notes.manas-2010:p0711:b001:l015: Laugh-to-weep escalation retained, although it reverses the ostensible command.
notes.manas-2010:p0711:b001:l025: Күлдүр and Чалыбай treated as personal names, Küldür and Chalybay.
notes.manas-2010:p0711:b001:l030: Аксакал бай treated provisionally as rich Aksakal, father of Aralbay; a descriptive white-bearded rich man remains possible.
notes.manas-2010:p0712:b001:l008: The snake sucking-dry simile is retained literally.
notes.manas-2010:p0712:b001:l013: Мурадына жетиптир literally says he attained his desire. Possible irony in the flight report is not converted into the opposite statement.
notes.manas-2010:p0712:b001:l016: Кызылдай provisionally rendered stark naked in the flight formula; figurative utter exposure/desperate flight is possible.
notes.manas-2010:p0712:b001:l019: Окоро түйгөн describes reins knotted short; the following row explicitly puts them between the riders' teeth.
notes.manas-2010:p0712:b001:l026: Алеңгир is destructive/deadly in1969/2015 dictionaries. Сыр жебе2015 admits sharp-pointed, smooth, or painted arrows; smooth selected here, not a secret message. Precise arrow finish remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0712:b001:l030: Womanlike is the scouts' gendered insult in the source; retained without endorsement.
notes.manas-2010:p0712:b001:l032: Black earth is the literal contemptuous contrast with a warrior, not silently replaced by another personal insult.
notes.manas-2010:p0713:b001:l001: The invocation of the fathers' graves is a curse, not an omitted exclamation.
notes.manas-2010:p0713:b001:l021: The sixty is explicit beside the forty formula and is not normalized.
notes.manas-2010:p0713:b001:l022: Байдын уулу provisionally treated as Bay's son, a patronymic formula; the literal rich man's son also remains possible.
notes.manas-2010:p0713:b001:l028: Жаман айтса таңылбас translated literally as not bound by an evil word. The elliptical syntax and exact proverbial force remain uncertain; no claim of a settled idiom.
notes.manas-2010:p0713:b001:l030: Карсак denotes the small steppe fox; generic fox used in the verse, rather than an unverified dog or wolf.
notes.manas-2010:p0713:b001:l038: Leaning on elbows is the concrete rest posture, retained alongside the no-sleep injunction.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l002: Сары изине чөп салып is a pursuit formula. Literal grass/yellow-trail image retained with the pursuit in the following row; its idiomatic force is relentless tracking, not a documented ritual.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l004: Parallel bare/pale-trail and grass image retained with the pursuit in the following row.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l012: Каканчын retained as the epic regional name Kakanchyn; no exact modern boundary is imposed.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l020: Көп көңүлү read as great pride in the humbling formula.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l026: Алда is God here, distinct from an ordinary deception verb.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l029: The tiger is the heroic metaphor; the possessive reference remains implicit.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l031: Даңгыт is a large dog here, not the Tangut ethnonym. Edition glossary1836:l028 and1969 dictionary with the ErToshtuk formula support the canine sense.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l036: Winning a prize/being covered in dust retained as the literal successful outcome.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l038: Dragging lead ropes/being covered in blood retained as the opposed defeat image; кан is not emended to khan.
notes.manas-2010:p0714:b001:l041: Бел is figurative support/strength to face the enemy, not necessarily an anatomical waist.
notes.manas-2010:p0715:b001:l005: Кылым rendered nations in the martial address, not an exact temporal century.
notes.manas-2010:p0715:b001:l016: Сайып with бак read as planting a garden, paired with building houses. Broader metaphoric skill is possible; no textual emendation.
notes.manas-2010:p0715:b001:l020: The stark give-up-your-lives address to companions is retained; the source does not explicitly readdress the enemy here.
notes.manas-2010:p0715:b001:l027: Бойлогон rendered advanced in the spear movement; not assigned an unprinted target.
notes.manas-2010:p0715:b001:l036: Шумдук covers extraordinary/astonishing happenings here, not restricted to moral evil.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l001: Жер союлуп is literally earth stripped/skinned; the exposed-earth image is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l011: Сыр найза: painted spear, unlike the several admitted senses of сыр жебе at712:l026.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l016: Same relentless-pursuit formula as714:l002, retaining the literal trail-and-grass image.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l018: Parallel bare/pale-trail formula retained; not omitted as repetition.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l023: Эгиз literally twins; the parallel warriors are rendered twin warriors without inventing biological relationships.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l024: Дүмөк read as a massed battle tumult; exact formation is not specified.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l031: Those remaining after the dead retains the compressed survivor construction.
notes.manas-2010:p0716:b001:l041: Бажы rendered tribute in the conquest context; no modern customs tariff is imposed.
notes.manas-2010:p0717:b001:l013: Көзүн салуу in this elimination context rendered wipe out, rather than adding literal eye-gouging.
notes.manas-2010:p0717:b001:l022: Moon-yellow is the source's plain-color image, retained literally.
notes.manas-2010:p0717:b001:l030: Бурчтанып rendered forming distant corners in the hazy landscape; exact visual topography remains provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0717:b001:l031: Учтанып rendered narrowing to points, preserving the paired indistinct landscape image.
notes.manas-2010:p0717:b001:l035: Сан кол read as countless host, a comparison with Bakay's effectiveness; no numerical troop addition.
notes.manas-2010:p0717:b001:l042: Какшаал retained as Kakshaal, the landscape beginning here continues on the next PDF page. No sentence-ending closure is invented.
notes.manas-2010:p0700:b001:l001: Ак үйлүү translated literally as white dwelling. Manas encyclopedia gives both political hostage and a symbol of wealth/power. Here Alöökö rules and takes tribute, favoring the authority/wealth image; no hostage status asserted. Exact institutional meaning remains unresolved. Coordinated with preceding678–697 batch; this is a qualified interpretation, not a settled historical identification.

transcription_check.scope: All twenty PDF page images visually inspected. Each page has42verse display rows,840total. No headings, prose or unresolved-source exclusions in this range. Parenthesized verse709:l005 included. Raw unchanged; no manuscript collation.

alignment_check.method: All840ordered Kyrgyz/English pairs read after drafting in two420-row groups. Dictionary corrections and qualified readings reread at their source positions. Same-agent review only.
